Reality (WebSearch-confirmed against trinodb/trino #21457 + trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html): `ARRAY_AGG(col)` over the single NULL-padded LEFT-JOIN unmatched row returns **`ARRAY[null]`** (one-element array containing NULL), NOT NULL and NOT `[]`. So the popular `COALESCE` guard never fires — the aggregate result is non-NULL. The official Trino aggregate docs explicitly call out this exact case verbatim: 'A common and very useful example is to use FILTER to remove nulls from consideration when using array_agg: `SELECT array_agg(name) FILTER (WHERE name IS NOT NULL) FROM region;`'. GREP FINDINGS for FIX B (`grep -rn 'array_agg|ARRAY_AGG|COALESCE(ARRAY|ARRAY\[\]|FILTER (WHERE' resources/`): many hits but ZERO that endorse `COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(x), ARRAY[])` as a no-match guard. The one-liner at r23:921 already correctly states `array_agg` is unordered unless specified. The §7A ARRAY_AGG references in r27 (lines 2880-3017) cover LISTAGG migration with correct `FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL)` hint at line 2904. **VERDICT: the responder's ineffective `COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(x), ARRAY[])` claim was a PURE FABRICATION — not present in any resource.** The gap: no resource had the explicit, keyword-anchored warning that LEFT-JOIN unmatched groups produce `ARRAY[null]` (not NULL) so `COALESCE` never fires. **FIX B EDIT (reconcile-in-place at r07:133-137, NEW §1a.2 sub-section inserted immediately after §1a.1 clause-order rule and BEFORE the `---` divider that introduces §2 Funnels — natural neighbor since array_agg is the reverse of UNNEST)**: ADDED §1a.2 `ARRAY_AGG over LEFT-JOIN unmatched groups returns ARRAY[null], NOT NULL and NOT [] — use FILTER (WHERE col IS NOT NULL)`.
